messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT ALERT - sev2 - serving-runtime memory growth detected in eu-west-2a pool (autodetect). Multiple container restarts reported. Please ack and triage. /incident INC-3078 :rotating_light:

maya: acked. noticing repeated OOMs on node gpu-23. seeing CUDA OOM + container crash loops. scaling still in progress. tagging simon.

simon: on it. grabbing logs now. suspecting KV cache fragmentation + paged-attention allocator slow leak. can someone grab a pod log and pmap?

maya: pasted pod logs from pod-serve-67:
```
I0315 03:41:12.812 RuntimeServe.cpp:421] allocating KV cache slab id=14 size=4194304
E0315 03:42:03.149 MemoryManager.cpp:88] CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY: failed alloc 256MB on device 0
W0315 03:42:03.150 Allocator.cpp:201] paged-alloc: fragment_count=4825 total_free=1.9GB total_used=30.1GB
E0315 03:42:03.151 Watchdog: killing process for OOM
```

maya: kubectl get pods -n redwood-serving --selector=pool=eu-west-2a -o wide:
```
NAME                     READY  STATUS   RESTARTS   AGE
pod-serve-65             1/1    Running  0          6h
pod-serve-66             0/1    CrashLoopBackOff  4  3h
pod-serve-67             0/1    CrashLoopBackOff  12 2h
pod-serve-68             1/1    Running  0  4h
```

maya: customer-facing routes for team-c have seen elevated 5xx rates (10% -> 40%) starting ~03:41 UTC. CS pinged.

eli: thanks, maya. I'm on customer impact. Team-c reported latency spikes and failed completions. collecting request ids for correlated traces. will update PG ticket.

simon: quick triage notes: allocator metrics show "paged_frag_count" increasing steadily on nodes with long up-times. GC isn't reclaiming small KV slabs because free segments are too fragmented to coalesce. leak likely in attention-paged cache path where ephemeral KV entries aren't freed on early exit.

tara: mitigation proposal (short):
- disable KV caching on pool eu-west-2a via runtime flag (fast toggle, no restart)
- set `attention_paging_threshold` to 0.7 -> reduce paging churn
- force traffic to fallback model variant (smaller KV footprint) via routing weight shift (canary route)
- cordon + drain most impacted nodes and restart runtime pods to reclaim memory

simon: +1 to disabling KV cache immediately. how do we toggle in prod?

maya: ops playbook: run `curl -X POST https://control-plane/api/v1/pools/eu-west-2a/flags -d '{"kv_cache_enabled":false}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'` (we have a short-lived toggle). I'll apply now.

maya: applied toggle at 03:44:12 UTC. watching metrics.

infra-bot: FLAG CHANGE: kv_cache_enabled set to false for pool eu-west-2a by maya at 2026-03-15T03:44:12Z.

maya: routing control: shifting 60% of team-c traffic to eu-central-1 safe-pool. command: `./routingctl shift --from eu-west-2a --to eu-central-1 --weight 60 --service team-c`

ryan: oncall takeover in 20m. handing off once we have stabilization.

simon: after toggle, we should proactively reduce page allocator threshold. sending patch to runtime config: `attention_paging_threshold=0.65` and reload config via control plane (no restart).

maya: reloaded threshold at 03:47:05 UTC.

maya: metrics update: paged-alloc free pool increasing, fragment_count plateauing. CrashLoopBackOff pod-serve-67 restarted cleanly and is now Running (1/1). 5xx for team-c down to ~6% from 40%.

eli: relaying to team-c: degraded period ~03:41-03:48 UTC, affected completions ~2.4k requests, ~1.9k failures. Customer SLA: interactive apps degraded. CS will offer post-incident note.

simon: digging into heap profiles from pod-serve-66. found many small KV slabs (~4KB) that are marked used but not referenced by active sessions. suspect double-free path missed on early-oom abort. capturing heap diff.

maya: I scheduled a rolling restart for older nodes with high fragment counts. command used: `kubectl drain gpu-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` then node reboot. Doing one at a time.

simon: confirm we'll want a hotfix in next deploy: ensure KV slab free path runs in the abort/exception branch and add a periodic coalescer to defrag small slabs. Also add a metric to expose per-slab reference counts.

tara: quick mitigation checklist copied to thread for handoff:
1) kv_cache_enabled=false (done)
2) attention_paging_threshold lowered (done)
3) route 60% traffic away (done)
4) drain and reboot nodes with fragment_count > 4000 (in progress)
5) restart pods that crash-loop (in progress)
6) enable extra GC pass in runtime via `RUNTIME_FORCE_GC=1` env toggle for new pods

maya: enabling `RUNTIME_FORCE_GC=1` in the daemonset template, will roll out with maxUnavailable=1 to avoid capacity loss.

infra-bot: DEPLOY STARTED: runtime config rollout by maya at 03:55:02Z (daemonset runtime-config).

maya: roll out succeeded, GC env toggle present. observing memory stabilize across nodes. fragmentation metrics slowly decline.

simon: collecting a reproducible unit test for the leak. I can repro with a stress script that simulates aborted attention requests with early termination. will open PR with failing test.

eli: customer update prepared. will send now and attach mitigations + timeline.

ryan: taking the thread. thanks for quick response. I'll monitor through the night and coordinate the dev fix deploy once PR is ready. leaving a note for morning shift to validate slab refcount metric added to canary.

maya: handing off full state to ryan. Incident INC-3078 -> mitigated but postmortem required. I'm un-acking at 04:10 UTC.

ryan: ack. adding to oncall journal and creating postmortem ticket. please upload heap diffs and the failing unit test link when available.

simon: opening PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/4226 (WIP) - includes added free path and periodic coalescer. will link CI once green.

eli: CS note posted to customer channel and PROD issue created.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: INC-3078 status=mitigated severity=sev2 assigned=ryan.

ryan: closing handoff. leaving monitoring alarms to default for 6h. will regroup in postmortem. good work team. :clap:
